item.title: Tk 1.21C robbery from PM’s cousin’s petrol pump: Five arrested
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) has arrested five people over the robbery of Tk 1.21 crore from a petrol pump in Uttara, allegedly linked to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s maternal cousin Tasin Akhtar Haque.
Police also recovered RAB-marked vests, fake identity cards, firearms and other equipment allegedly used in the robbery. The suspected mastermind remains at large.
The arrestees are: Md Ilias Shikdar, 36, Jafar, 36, Md Rabiul Islam alias Rubel, 34, Mintu Rari, 23, and Sagar Baroi, 40.
Additional Police Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Saturday.
He said four employees of DL Filling Station were carrying Tk 1.21 crore to a bank around 10:30am on August 9 when a group of motorcycle-borne robbers intercepted them near Crown Plaza on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Road.
The robbers allegedly threatened and assaulted them with firearms and machetes before fleeing with the money.
Following the incident, the DB and Uttara Crime Division launched a joint investigation. Acting on intelligence, police arrested Ilias Shikdar and Jafar in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj.
Police later recovered three RAB-marked vests, two caps, fake RAB identity cards, number plates, walkie-talkies, handcuffs, two 7.65mm pistols, three magazines and six rounds of ammunition from Ilias’s rented home in Bandar.
Rubel and Mintu were subsequently arrested in Matuail and Kazlarpar, respectively. Police recovered Tk 3 lakh in stolen cash from Rubel’s residence, while a raid on Mintu’s home yielded four RAB-marked vests, fake RAB IDs, number plates, walkie-talkies, handcuffs, two pistols, three magazines and 15 rounds of ammunition.
Based on information provided by Rubel and Mintu, police arrested Sagar from his rented home in Postogola and recovered Tk 9 lakh in stolen cash. Shafiqul Islam said the stolen money was divided among the gang, with the masterminds taking larger shares and others receiving portions for providing logistical support. Sagar received Tk 9 lakh but had not spent it, he added.
The DB chief said ballistic checks showed that the recovered firearms were not weapons looted from police but had been illegally acquired.
He said the mastermind remains at large and that investigators had found no prior personal connection between the suspect and the victim.
According to police, the gang targeted the petrol pump after learning that several days’ cash had accumulated because banks were closed during the holidays. The group allegedly planned the robbery knowing the money would be deposited once the banks reopened.
Police said efforts are underway to arrest the remaining suspects and recover the rest of the stolen money.

item.title: Bangladesh, Kosovo reaffirm strong opposition to all forms of transnational crimes
item.description:
Recognizing their common commitment to peace, stability, and international security, Bangladesh and Kosovo have reaffirmed their strong opposition to terrorism, violent extremism, and all forms of transnational crime.
They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the friendly relations between the two countries on the basis of mutual respect, shared values, common interests, and the principles of international law.
The issues of mutual interest were discussed at the second Foreign Office Consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora of the Republic of Kosovo held in Prishtina recently.
The Bangladeshi delegation was led by Dr M Nazrul Islam, secretary (Bilateral – East & West) of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while the Kosovar delegation was led by Ilir Muçaj, secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora.
The two sides acknowledged the significant untapped potential for expanding bilateral cooperation in the fields of trade, investment, education, agriculture, information and communication technology, tourism, labour mobility, and people-to-people exchanges.
They agreed to continue working closely to fully utilise the complementarities of their respective economies for mutual benefit.
The two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and expressed satisfaction with the steady progress achieved since the establishment of diplomatic relations, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Both sides welcomed the bilateral instruments concluded thus far and emphasized their importance in strengthening institutional cooperation.
They agreed that bilateral relations would be further enhanced through the early conclusion of the agreements currently under negotiation, particularly those related to economic cooperation, the avoidance of double taxation, and other mutually beneficial areas.
The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing cooperation at both the bilateral and multilateral levels and agreed to continue close coordination and consultation in regional and international organizations on issues of mutual interest.
The Kosovo side highly appreciated Bangladesh's longstanding contribution to United Nations peacekeeping operations and expressed its sincere gratitude to the members of the Bangladesh to the UN Peace-Keeping Forces who served in Kosovo.
The Bangladeshi side welcomed Kosovo's growing participation in international and regional organizations and initiatives and expressed its support for Kosovo's continued integration into international organizations, conventions, and multilateral mechanisms as an equal participant.
The Kosovo side commended Bangladesh for its humanitarian response to the Rohingya refugee crisis and expressed its support for Bangladesh's efforts aimed at ensuring the safe, voluntary, dignified, and sustainable repatriation of the displaced Rohingya population to Rakhine State in Myanmar.
The Kosovo side also underlined the importance of sustained engagement by the international community to facilitate a durable solution to the crisis.
The two sides recognized the growing demand for labour mobility and underlined the importance of establishing a structured framework for the recruitment and employment of Bangladeshi workers in Kosovo.
They agreed to explore the possibility of developing government-to-government (G2G) cooperation mechanisms that would ensure transparent, orderly, and mutually beneficial labour migration.
The two sides emphasized the importance of maintaining regular Foreign Office Consultations as an effective mechanism for strengthening bilateral cooperation, reviewing progress, and identifying new areas of collaboration.
They agreed to hold the third Foreign Office Consultations in Dhaka during 2027 at a mutually convenient date.
The consultations were held in a constructive atmosphere, reflecting the excellent relations between the Republic of Kosovo and the People's Republic of Bangladesh and their shared commitment to further deepening bilateral cooperation.
